newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Nov 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Nov 5.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
China is mulling cutting fees for international telephone calls by the end of this year or early next year. Authorities are also considering raising domestic telephone and mail rates.
President Jiang Zemin calls for relieving rural poverty by the year 2000.
Propaganda chief Ding Guangen says paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's theories form the basis for promoting socialist ethics and correct ideologies.
A circular issued by the People's Bank of China, the central bank, orders non-banking financial institutions to re-register.
The State Information Centre says China will harness direct foreign investment of $50 billion is 1997.
Industrial growth is forecast to be between 13 and 14 percent in 1997 because of investment growth.
